name: Shirtmasters
old_description: We put quality and care before all else ensuring that our clients have what they need to outfit their employees, look good on a family vacation or promote their event in a memorable way.
about:
Shirtmasters operates from Chichester, New Hampshire, just outside Concord. The company has served the custom apparel market for over 30 years, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed. Ownership details and founder names have not been shared.

The business provides screen printing, embroidery, and promotional product services through in-house production departments. A graphic design team supports custom artwork, and the company sources blank apparel from over 100 brands. Typical orders range from single-name embroidery on uniforms to multi-color screen prints on hundreds of shirts.

Clients include sports teams, corporations, municipalities, schools and universities, small businesses, and restaurants. The company also supplies decorated apparel for trade shows and events across New England and nationally.

Shirtmasters emphasizes personal service, environmental consciousness, and community involvement as core differentiators. The company cites a typical turnaround of two weeks or less for most of the year, with dedicated sales representatives guiding customers through brand selection and design. Its stated mission stresses quality service, putting customers first, being conscious of the environment, and helping the local New Hampshire community.

name: Shore Customs Car and Truck Accessories
old_description: Shore Customs is the Jersey Shore’s Premier Source for Professional Car & Truck Customization
about:
Shore Customs Car and Truck Accessories operates in Ocean Township, New Jersey, serving the Jersey Shore region as a vehicle customization shop. The business focuses on professional car and truck accessory installation and customization.

The shop provides a full line of automotive customization services including 3M ceramic coating, paint protection film, window tinting, auto detailing, audio systems and electronics (GPS, Pioneer radios, Sirius XM), remote start, radar detectors, auto security, rim repairs, powder coating, vinyl wraps, WeatherTech mats, Rhino Linings, lift kits, new rims and tires, tonneau covers, truck accessories, Jeep accessories, Front Runner outfitting, Kargo Master vehicle shelving, frame repair, and Katzkin leather and heated seating installations. Customers receive detailed project reports with a breakdown of services performed.

The company serves individual vehicle owners, including Jeep and truck enthusiasts, off-road adventurers, and commercial users needing vehicle shelving. Testimonials reference work on a 2018 Toyota Tacoma with Katzkin seat covers and heaters, as well as window tinting and remote start installations for daily drivers.

Shore Customs emphasizes transparent communication and careful, step-by-step work, guaranteeing customer satisfaction on completed projects. Financing is available up to $10,000 for larger customization jobs.

name: Sider's Woodcrafting
old_description: Please contact us if you cannot find what you are looking for!
about:
Sider's Woodcrafting operates from a home-based workshop in Brewer, Maine. The company was founded in October 2015 by Bruce and Mary Graybill after the birth of their first child prompted them to seek ways to save money. Bruce began making cutting boards as Christmas gifts using only a table saw and a belt sander; a friend's request for eleven more boards sparked the business.

The shop produces handcrafted cutting boards, end-grain chopping blocks, charcuterie boards, specialty shaped boards, epoxy coasters, and desk accessories. All items are made by hand in the small workshop beside the Graybills' house, using domestic and exotic woods sourced worldwide along with epoxy resin. In its first full year (2016), the company sold nearly 400 cutting boards.

Sider's Woodcrafting sells directly to consumers through its online store, serving the kitchenware and home-goods markets. Customers include home cooks, gift buyers, and enthusiasts of functional wood art. The product line ranges from small cheese boards to two-foot-long "mega" cutting boards and custom epoxy-inlaid pieces.

The Graybills emphasize turning everyday objects into functional works of art that showcase the natural color and grain of the wood. The business remains family-owned, with Bruce as owner and Mary providing support, alongside a small team of assistants and specialists.

name: Sierra Components Inc
old_description: Sierra Components adds Component Design, Packaging and more to our list of services.
about:
Sierra Components Inc. was founded in 1992 in Minden, Nevada, as a family-run business serving the microelectronics industry. What began with a fax machine, a flow hood, and a few nitrogen boxes has grown into a multi-million-dollar distribution and processing facility specializing in silicon wafers and bare die. The company's president and founder brings over 40 years of bare-die distribution experience and more than 42 years in the microelectronics field.

Today the firm operates as a distribution and processing center, offering visual inspection to MIL-STD-883 Method 2010 and MIL-STD-750 Methods 2072/2073, element evaluation and lot qualification to MIL-PRF-38534D Levels H and K, MIL-PRF-19500, and customer source-control drawings. It also provides alternate-component sourcing, wafer processing such as SAW sort and inspection of wafers to die form and wafer probe, and a surplus-inventory program that stores and sells excess stock with a guaranteed return of at least 50 percent of book value. A partnership with Kooker Technologies adds component design, packaging, and substrate fabrication with fast turnaround times.

Sierra Components serves the microelectronics and semiconductor sectors, including customers who require military-grade qualification to MIL-PRF-38534D and MIL-PRF-19500. Its client base includes original equipment manufacturers and other buyers needing bare-die distribution, wafer-level processing, and obsolescence management.

The founder's stated goal has been to provide top-notch service with a personal touch—no automated attendants, just a real person on the phone. The company describes itself as large enough to handle the task yet small enough to give each customer individual attention, a philosophy reinforced by a staff with over 78 combined years in the semiconductor industry.

name: Sierra Peaks Corporation
old_description: Building creative engineering and manufacturing solutions for every customer
about:
Sierra Peaks Corporation is headquartered in Albuquerque, New Mexico, with additional facilities in Fairfax, Virginia, and Lemon Grove, California. The company has been designing, engineering, and manufacturing custom system solutions for over four decades, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed. Ownership details and founder names have not been shared in available materials.

The firm provides full-service engineering and manufacturing, spanning mechanical, electrical, systems, and software design through to machining, welding, electromechanical assembly, modeling, sewing, and custom cable fabrication. Its three sites collectively offer more than 50,000 square feet of manufacturing and program management space, all maintained to NISPOM security standards for restricted programs. Capabilities also include first-article prototyping, inspection simulations, and integration services.

Sierra Peaks serves the defense, intelligence, aerospace, maritime, energy, audio, and research sectors, with highlighted work in national security and aerospace. Customers range from government agencies to commercial organizations requiring highly customized hardware and software solutions, such as aerostructures, automated test equipment, and specialized particulate sampling systems.

The company emphasizes that no two solutions are alike, positioning its differentiation on end-to-end collaboration—from concept and line drawings through prototyping, production, and testing—delivered on time and on budget by dedicated project managers. Its facilities are configured for rapid prototyping, manufacturing, and testing under security clearances.

name: Signet Plastics
old_description: Precision plastic manufacturing with over 30 years of experience
about:
Signet Plastics was founded in 1996 and is headquartered in Maryville, Tennessee. The company describes itself as a processor of plastics with over 30 years of industry experience, though it does not disclose its founders or ownership structure publicly.

Signet Plastics provides custom plastic injection molding services for manufacturers requiring precision, consistency, and dependable delivery. Its capabilities include overmolding, hot stamping, pad printing, tooling and part design, as well as assembly and secondary operations, all backed by quality and process control programs. The company has not published details on facility size, employee count, or annual production volumes.

The company serves a diverse client base across automotive, medical, consumer, and industrial applications, producing high-quality molded plastic components tailored to each sector's requirements.

Signet Plastics emphasizes that its reputation is built on service excellence and a commitment to providing the highest quality, with a goal not just to meet but to exceed customer expectations. It positions itself as a partner in its customers' success rather than merely a plastics processor.

name: Silkhands Inc.
old_description: we have helped independent and emerging designers create fashion. We specialize in Quality and Efficiency and are 100% made in Los Angeles.
about:
Silkhands Inc. operates from Los Angeles, California, and was founded in 2006. The company began as a fashion development and production house focused on helping independent and emerging designers bring their designs to life.

The facility provides end-to-end garment manufacturing services, including pattern making, sample development, fabric cutting, pattern grading, marker making, production sewing, finishing, inspection, pressing, steaming, folding, bagging, labeling, and boxing. All work is performed in-house by the company's staff, with production cut on-site and sent to sewing and finishing departments.

Silkhands serves independent and emerging designers across a range of apparel categories, including men's, women's, teen's, and baby apparel, as well as men's and women's swimwear, men's underwear, and delicate lingerie. The company acts as a one-stop shop, guiding clients through each step from pattern to finished goods.

The company emphasizes quality and efficiency, highlighting its 100% Los Angeles-based production, contractual guarantees on specifications and delivery dates, and a standard production lead time of four to eight weeks.

name: Simcona Electronics Corporation
old_description: sourcing, inventory management, or control panel manufacturing challenges
about:
Simcona Electronics Corporation was founded in 1962 by Louis Iacona and Simon Braitman in Rochester, New York. The family-owned business began as a component distribution company operating from an 1,800-square-foot loft opposite Kodak Park. Leadership transitioned to the second generation in 1999, and Marc Iacona acquired sole ownership in 2011.

Today the company operates across three facilities totaling 130,000 square feet and employs more than 70 people. Simcona provides three core services: build-to-print industrial control panel manufacturing certified to UL 508A and UL 698, electronic component distribution leveraging a network of over 200 suppliers, and cable and wire solutions sourced from manufacturers such as Southwire, Belden, and Lapp. Capabilities include prototyping, high-mix/low-volume and scalable production runs, engineering support with DFM recommendations, AI-enabled procurement, kitting, inventory management, and 100% functional testing under an ISO 9001:2015 quality system.

Customers span aerospace, healthcare, military, data infrastructure, commercial entertainment, industrial, and oil and gas sectors. Testimonials reference clients in each of these verticals, and the company primarily serves the eastern United States.

Simcona emphasizes long-term relationships, guided by core values of caring, collaboration, passion, loyalty, innovation, and integrity. The firm invests in Lean Six Sigma training, project management certification, and purpose-built facilities to maintain a specialist workforce and a resilient supplier ecosystem.

Items feature materials such as koa wood, Italian acrylic, resin, glass, sterling silver, pearls, and aluminum. The operation includes a physical workshop and gallery open by appointment, but no manufacturing processes, facility size, headcount, or production volumes are provided.

The customer base appears to be retail consumers seeking Hawaiian gifts and art, with the stated mission of promoting the islands' cultural heritage and empowering local artisans. The gallery markets its collection globally through its website.

The business emphasizes its Hawaiian roots and the authenticity of its curated collection as its defining purpose, aiming to spread the aloha spirit worldwide.
